facts.text: Quebec City’s name comes from the Algonquian word Kébec, meaning “where the river narrows” at the Saint Lawrence’s promontory.
Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec City on July 3, 1608, establishing the first permanent French settlement in North America.
In 1541 Jacques Cartier founded Fort Charlesbourg‑Royal, Quebec City’s earliest French settlement, which was abandoned after a harsh winter.
The 1759 Battle of the Plains of Abraham in Quebec City ended French rule and shifted North America’s balance of power.
Old Quebec, a UNESCO World Heritage site, offers a walkable, safe historic core that feels like stepping back in time.
The 4.6‑km Promenade Samuel‑De Champlain runs along the Saint Lawrence, linking the city’s eastern and western waterfronts.
